title: The Faint sound from the yard
subtitle: 安全预防 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）
meta: 主题语境：安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）　|　核心词汇：faint　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 faint 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the keeper wrote of ① a faint sound from the yard in the calendar, and everybody in the tower said at once that it was ② fainter than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the keeper, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the faint ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the faintest sound from the yard anybody in the tower had ever seen, or so the calendar for January 1980 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too faint to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the faint ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a faint smell of smoke, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as faint as the smell of smoke they had once had in the old tower. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was faint or not, and he said so.

By 1993 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the calendar. What the line asked for was ⑦ something faint, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next tower called the whole plan ⑧ quite faint; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the calendar kept the names of the faint ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1996, at once, she wrote of another faint sound from the yard in the same calendar, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ fainter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The faintest smell of smoke in the whole tower, she said in 1998, was the one she could never quite name; the faint ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 微弱（前置定语 a faint sound from the yard：1986 年守夜人在年历里记下的那件微弱的微响）
B. adj. 微弱／模糊（比较级 fainter than：文中两处，一处比院里传来的微响，一处比预想）
C. adj. 微弱／模糊（最高级 the faintest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 微弱（表语 too faint to do：母亲觉得它太微弱，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 模糊（前置定语 a faint smell of smoke：叔叔把整件事称作一桩模糊的烟味）
F. adj. 模糊（同级比较 as faint as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩淡淡的烟味相比）
G. adj. 模糊（后置定语 something faint：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 模糊（受程度副词修饰 quite faint：那位过路人的评价）

items.q: a faint sound from the yard
the faintest sound from the yard anybody
The faintest smell of smoke in

answers.why: faint 意为“微弱”，1986 年守夜人在年历里记下的是“一件微弱的微响”，此处作前置定语 a faint sound from the yard。
faint 意为“微弱”，此处用比较级 fainter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
faint 意为“微弱”，年历上 一月 那行字说它是钟楼里最微弱的一件，故用最高级 the faintest sound from the yard。
faint 意为“微弱”，母亲认为这件东西“太微弱了，谁也用不上”，too faint to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
faint 意为“模糊”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩模糊的烟味”，此处作前置定语 a faint smell of smoke。
faint 意为“模糊”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩淡淡的烟味一样模糊”，同级比较用 as faint as。
faint 意为“模糊”，年历上那半行字要的是“模糊的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something faint。
faint 意为“模糊”，邻钟楼来的那位过路人认为这套计划“相当模糊”，quite 修饰原级 faint。
faint 意为“模糊”，1996 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要模糊”，故用比较级 fainter than。
faint 意为“模糊”，母亲 1998 年说的是“整个钟楼里最模糊的那一桩”，故用最高级 the faintest smell of smoke。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1986 年，守夜人在年历里记下了一件微弱的微响。（a faint sound from the yard）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更微弱。（fainter than …）
母亲觉得它太微弱，谁也用不上。（too faint to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩模糊的烟味。（a faint smell of smoke）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩淡淡的烟味一样模糊。（as faint as …）
到了 1993 年，年历上只剩半行字：要的是一件模糊的东西。（something faint）
answers: In 1986 the keeper wrote of a faint sound from the yard in the calendar.
Everybody said it was fainter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too faint to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a faint smell of smoke.
He said nobody would call it as faint as the smell of smoke they had once had.
By 1993 the calendar asked for nothing but something faint.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 faint 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1986 the keeper wrote of a faint sound from the yard in the calendar, and nobody forgot it.
It was the faintest sound from the yard in the tower, or so the calendar says.
My mother thought it too faint to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a faint smell of smoke, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next tower called the plan quite faint, and everybody laughed.
The faint ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
